html:
The Kabul airlift was the evacuation by air of more than 120,000 people from Kabul in the last two weeks of August 2021, after the Taliban took over Afghanistan.

The United States had agreed with the Taliban in the Doha Agreement of 2020 to withdraw its troops. As they left, the Afghan army collapsed and the Taliban entered Kabul on 15 August. Foreigners and Afghans who had worked with Western forces rushed to the airport. Huge crowds pressed at the gates, and some people clung to a departing American plane and fell to their deaths.

American and allied soldiers held the airport while military planes flew people out day and night. On 26 August a suicide bomber of the Islamic State Khorasan Province struck a crowd at the Abbey Gate, killing about 170 Afghans and 13 American soldiers. The last American plane left on 30 August, ending the twenty-year war. Many Afghans who had worked with the West were left behind, and another wave of the Afghan refugee exodus began.
sum: The Kabul airlift was the evacuation by air of more than 120,000 people from Kabul in the last two weeks of August 2021, after the Taliban took over Afghanistan.
